tagline: Ghana's golden-coast capital — Makola's market maze, Labadi's beach drums, and the city behind the 'Year of Return' diaspora welcome.
overview: Accra has become the gateway for the African diaspora's homecoming — the 'Year of Return' (2019) and 'Beyond the Return' drew hundreds of thousands of visitors tracing ancestry and culture to Ghana's coast.

The city itself rewards days: Makola Market's organised chaos, the fishing canoes and boxing gyms of Jamestown beneath its lighthouse, Independence Square's Black Star Gate, and Labadi Beach's drummers and horses at dusk.

Speed's 2025 Africa stop streamed from Accra to big crowds. The food is the memory that stays — banku and grilled tilapia, red red (beans and plantain), and the jollof that fuels a friendly war with Lagos.

funFacts.title: THE YEAR OF RETURN
funFacts.text: 2019 marked 400 years since the first enslaved Africans reached Virginia — Ghana invited the diaspora home and they came.

funFacts.title: BLACK STAR GATE
funFacts.text: Independence Square's monument honours Ghana's 1957 freedom — first in sub-Saharan Africa.

funFacts.title: MAKOLA'S MAZE
funFacts.text: Makola Market is run largely by women traders — a labyrinth of fabric, food and everything.

funFacts.title: JAMESTOWN'S LIGHTHOUSE
funFacts.text: The 1930s lighthouse overlooks fishing canoes and Ghana's boxing-gym heartland.

funFacts.title: THE JOLLOF WAR
funFacts.text: Ghana-vs-Nigeria jollof is West Africa's longest-running delicious dispute.

funFacts.title: KENTE COUNTRY
funFacts.text: Royal Ashanti kente cloth is woven nearby — every pattern carries a meaning.

funFacts.title: OXFORD STREET
funFacts.text: Osu's main strip is the centre for restaurants, bars and craft stalls.

funFacts.title: SLAVE-COAST HISTORY
funFacts.text: Cape Coast and Elmina castles, a day trip west, were the last African ground many ancestors touched.

funFacts.title: LABADI SUNDAYS
funFacts.text: Labadi Beach fills on weekends with drummers, dancers and horse rides.

funFacts.title: DU BOIS' HOUSE
funFacts.text: W.E.B. Du Bois spent his final years here — his house is now a memorial library.
